1.explanation: 1) ListBox.js takes any aria-controls/aria-owns passed in and blindly spreads them onto both the root and the toggle button, so when the menu is closed you still get broken IDrefs. Those props need to be filtered out or overridden based on isOpen. 2) ListBoxField.js hard-codes an aria-label of “open menu”/“close menu” on the clickable toggle <div>, which replaces the user’s visible placeholder text as the accessible name. 3) Dropdown.js simply passes all props through to ListBox (including those bad ARIA attributes) without any validation. Fixing these three files will allow you to drop invalid aria-controls/owns in the closed state and restore a proper accessible name that includes the visible label.
1.bug_scenario: When you render the Carbon React <Dropdown> with custom aria-controls and aria-owns props (or even in the closed state by default), those attributes end up on the toggle button pointing at an ID that doesn’t exist (e.g. “carbon-dropdown-example__menu”). Axe/DAP flags that as “ARIA attributes must conform to valid values.”  At the same time the internal toggle <div> (ListBoxField) carries an aria-label of “open menu” or “close menu,” which overrides its visible label text (the “Dropdown menu options” placeholder), causing “Accessible name does not contain the visible label text.”

2.explanation:
1) Dropdown.js is the public wrapper that takes your id, label, aria‐props and hands them off into the ListBox. It passes the id down into ListBox and ListBoxField, so any aria-controls/owns you give to Dropdown end up hard-coding the generated menu ID into ListBoxField.

2) ListBoxField.js is where the <div role="button" …> lives. It unconditionally renders aria-controls and aria-owns (using the id + "__menu" suffix) even when the menu isn’t mounted, so aria-controls points to a non-existent ID. It also sets aria-label to just “Open menu” or “Close menu,” which conflicts with the visible label text, so the accessible name doesn’t include the dropdown’s label.

3) ListBoxMenu.js is responsible for rendering the element with id = `${id}__menu` (the target of aria-controls/owns). That menu only exists in the DOM when you expand the dropdown—so when it’s closed there is no element with that generated ID. This mismatch triggers the “invalid ARIA attribute values” error in DAP/axe. To fix: only apply aria-controls/owns when the menu is present (or keep a hidden menu element), or move to aria-labelledby for the button, and merge the visible label text into the button’s accessible name rather than overriding it.
2.bug_scenario: When you render a Carbon React <Dropdown> and inspect it with DAP (or axe-core), you see two violations on the collapsed dropdown button: 1) aria-controls/aria-owns is pointing at an element ID (e.g. “carbon‐dropdown‐example__menu”) that doesn’t actually exist in the DOM when the menu is closed, and 2) the button’s aria-label (“Open menu” or “Close menu”) does not include the visible label text (“Dropdown menu options”), so its accessible name doesn’t match the visible label. Both of those ARIA problems are coming from the internal ListBoxField (and the way the menu ID is generated in ListBoxMenu) and the way Dropdown spreads user props into that field.
